_about: Newbury for tools/course/real/layout.py. Ring 0 = OSM's outer edge of the turf (point numbers on reference/newbury/plan-draft.png, lower panel). OSM's turf is about 55 m wide round the loop: the flat course outside and the jumps course inside, so the flat course's inside rail is taken 30 m in from the outer edge (offset 30). The spur at the far end (the round mile's chute) is narrow, so there the inside rail is its own west edge. Where the round course comes off the far bend it runs diagonally (north-west) into the straight course's inner side; the game's run-in is shared with the straight mile on the stands side, the round course's rail carrying on its diagonal into it. The 1m5f61y chute off the home bend is narrow: its inside rail starts 10 m in from its south edge.
